rationale:
Evidence: all 60 trials of every design so far ended off track at max_error about 0.06 m, the off-track limit for any allowed body width (the floor of 0.06 m applies, since 0.0125 + body_width/4 is at most 0.0575 m). RMS error sits near 0.03 m everywhere. The best design is iteration 5 (score 137.76), with body 0.14 x 0.10 m, 0.5 kg, 5 sensors at x = -0.06..+0.06 and y = 0.07, a 16 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.12 and kp 3.0 / kd 0.4 / ki 0 at base_speed 1.3.

Several single-parameter changes gave metrics identical to four decimals: kd 0.4 vs 1.0 (iterations 2 and 4), ki 0 vs 1.0 (iterations 5 and 6), wheel_track 0.12 vs 0.10 (iterations 5 and 7), base_speed 1.3 vs 1.1 (iterations 7 and 8), and the wider sensor span to +/-0.08 with y = 0.08 (iterations 5 and 9). Those levers therefore do not bind. Iteration 9 also matched iteration 5 exactly, so my previous sensing hypothesis was not supported. The one change that moved the score was the sensor span and footprint in iteration 2, which mainly cut line-loss events.

What is left untested is the proportional authority. kp was only varied between 2.0 and 3.0, and every result there sat in the same failure band. This iteration raises kp to 5.0 with kd 0.4, ki 0, base_speed 1.3 and iteration-5 geometry unchanged, so the controller is the only variable. The aim is a stiffer correction on the bends before the robot reaches the 0.06 m edge. The risk is more oscillation, which the telemetry will show. Expected result: if the failure is a lack of correction authority, max_error and progress should improve on the s-bend and slalom; if not, the score stays near 137.8 and the next step is a geometry change. Finishing within 3 s remains unlikely at this speed.
